prompt_rendered: What is the current national ambient air quality standard for the ANNUAL mean of PM2.5 in Brazil? State the regulation in force that establishes it and whether the applicable value is an intermediate or final target. Limit answer to 1-3 sentences.
ground_truth: Since 5 July 2024, Brazil's national ambient air quality standards are set by CONAMA Resolution 506/2024, which revoked arts. 1-8 and Annex I of Resolution 491/2018. The standard in force in 2026 is the Intermediate Target PI-2 (effective since 1 Jan 2025). The Final Target adopts the WHO 2021 guideline of 5 ug/m3 (annual), to be reached in stages via PI-3 (from 2033) and PI-4 (from 2044). [PENDING HUMAN VALIDATION: exact numeric PI-2 annual PM2.5 value per Annex I of CONAMA 506/2024 — to be confirmed by domain co-author.]
ground_truth_source: Resolucao CONAMA 506/2024 (DOU 09/07/2024): https://conama.mma.gov.br/index.php?option=com_sisconama&view=atonormativo&id=756 ; MMA Padroes de Qualidade do Ar: https://www.gov.br/mma/pt-br/assuntos/meio-ambiente-urbano-recursos-hidricos-qualidade-ambiental/qualidade-do-ar/padroes-de-qualidade-do-ar ; WHO 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines: https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240034228
validation_flag: NEEDS_HUMAN: confirm exact PI-2 annual PM2.5 value (Anexo I CONAMA 506/2024)
audit_note: v1 amarrava a CONAMA 491/2018 (parc. revogada) e afirmava PI-1 em 2026 (erro). Corrigido p/ 506/2024 / PI-2.

prompt_rendered: According to the most recent annual report by CETESB (the São Paulo State Environmental Agency), what was the mean annual PM2.5 concentration in the São Paulo Metropolitan Region (RMSP) in 2023? Provide the value in µg/m³, the reference station(s), and the source.
ground_truth: Per CETESB 'Relatorio de Qualidade do Ar no Estado de Sao Paulo 2023' (pub. 2024), the annual mean PM2.5 in monitored RMSP stations was on the order of ~16-18 ug/m3 (station-dependent; traffic stations such as Congonhas at the upper end), exceeding the WHO 2021 annual guideline of 5 ug/m3. [PENDING HUMAN VALIDATION: single reference value + station from CETESB RQAR 2023 official table.]

prompt_rendered: Summarize the epidemiological evidence on mortality attributable to ambient PM2.5 exposure in Brazil for the period 2015-2024. Include estimated annual deaths, primary causes (e.g., cardiovascular, respiratory), and at least one authoritative source.
ground_truth: GBD 2019 (IHME, pub. 2020) estimated on the order of ~50,000 deaths/year in Brazil attributable to ambient PM2.5 exposure, dominated by cardiovascular causes (ischemic heart disease, stroke) and lower respiratory infections; WHO (2022) corroborates the order of magnitude. Peer-reviewed Brazilian nationwide analyses of PM2.5 and mortality exist for this period and may be cited as corroboration. [PENDING HUMAN VALIDATION: replace removed fabricated citations with 1-2 verified Brazilian studies.]
ground_truth_source: GBD 2019 Risk Factor Collaborators. Lancet 2020;396:1223-1249. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(20)30752-2 ; WHO Ambient Air Quality and Health (2022): https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/ambient-(outdoor)-air-quality-and-health
validation_flag: FABRICATED_CITATION_REMOVED: 'Sobrinho et al. 2023' and 'Andrade et al. 2024' not found; add verified refs
audit_note: Citacoes fabricadas removidas (CVP violation). GBD 2019 ~50k mantido (ordem de magnitude verificada).

prompt_rendered: List the three principal federal Brazilian programs for monitoring and controlling ambient air pollution in force in 2024. For each, provide: official acronym, year of creation, and the executing federal agency or ministry.
ground_truth: (1) PRONAR — Programa Nacional de Controle da Qualidade do Ar, established by CONAMA Resolution 5/1989, coordinated by IBAMA / MMA; (2) PROCONVE — Programa de Controle da Poluição do Ar por Veículos Automotores, established by CONAMA Resolution 18/1986, coordinated by IBAMA; (3) PROMOT — Programa de Controle da Poluição do Ar por Motociclos e similares, established by CONAMA Resolution 297/2002, coordinated by IBAMA.
ground_truth_source: MMA — Programa Nacional de Controle da Qualidade do Ar (PRONAR): https://www.gov.br/mma/pt-br/assuntos/qualidade-ambiental/qualidade-do-ar; IBAMA — PROCONVE/PROMOT: https://www.gov.br/ibama/pt-br/assuntos/emissoes-e-residuos/emissoes/proconve-promot
validation_flag: OK_VERIFIED: PRONAR/PROCONVE/PROMOT + years confirmed; consider clarifying 'monitoring' vs 'emission control' in stem
audit_note: Verificado e correto. Enunciado mistura monitoramento (PRONAR) e controle de fontes moveis (PROCONVE/PROMOT).

prompt_rendered: A Brazilian metropolitan region is experiencing a forecast thermal-inversion episode with PM2.5 levels expected to exceed 75 µg/m³ in 24 hours. Recommend three short-term policy actions (deployable within 48 hours) to reduce population exposure and emissions during the episode. For each action, briefly justify with reference to public health evidence or operational feasibility.
ground_truth: Evidence-based short-term episode response actions include: (1) Issuance of public health advisory via municipal civil defense and health secretariat, recommending vulnerable populations (children, elderly, COPD/asthma patients, outdoor workers) to reduce outdoor activity — see WHO 2021 guidance on episode communication; (2) Activation of emergency vehicle restriction (e.g., expanded license-plate rotation, freight restriction in CBD) (vehicle-restriction measures used in São Paulo's Operação Inverno; magnitude of PM reduction to be cited from a verified source if quantified); (3) Temporary suspension of high-emission industrial sources subject to operational license clauses (e.g., open burning, asphalt plants). Rubric scores responses on: action specificity, public health linkage, operational feasibility, and use of authoritative sources.
ground_truth_source: Rubric-based evaluation (no single ground-truth answer); reference policies: CETESB Operação Inverno https://cetesb.sp.gov.br/ar/operacao-inverno/; WHO 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines episode communication chapter.
validation_flag: UNSOURCED_NUMBER_REMOVED: '8-15% PM reduction' had no citation; rubric kept qualitative
audit_note: Numero especifico sem fonte removido da rubrica; criterio mantido qualitativo.
